data.cultural_impact: The name Aejaz holds a strong cultural significance in the Islamic world as it signifies power, capability, and strength. It is a name often given to boys who are expected to grow up to be strong, capable, and powerful individuals. In some communities, the name is also associated with bravery, courage, and fearlessness, as these are qualities that are highly valued and revered.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Aejaz can be seen as a reminder of the power and capability that comes from faith in Allah. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) once said, "Allah is the Strong and Powerful," emphasizing the strength and power that comes from trusting and relying on God. The spiritual significance of the name is not just about personal strength and capability, but also about using that strength to serve and help others, thereby contributing to the betterment of the community and the world around us.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'Al-'Ibar', written in 1377 CE, describes Aejaz ibn Marwan as a Berber ruler of the Marinids who reigned over Morocco from 1351 to 1358 CE.
Al-Masudi, in his 'Muruj al-Dhahab' (The Meadows of Gold), mentions Ayyaz ibn Omar as a governor of Egypt under the Fatimid Caliphate during the late 10th century CE.
